text:
maya: noticing a bunch of multi-GPU training jobs in us-west-2 are suddenly thrashing — allreduce times spiked and NCCL reports ibverbs errors. started yesterday evening, still happening.
chen: which pool and NIC type? is this Dedicated or Private? any recent infra changes?
maya: dedicated-gpu-pool-3, machines are A100s on Mellanox NICs (mlx5). no recent kernel upgrades on nodes, but we did a switch firmware push in that region last week.
todd: can you paste the NCCL error? short snippet is fine.
maya: here are the relevant lines from one job:
```
NCCL WARN Call to ibv_post_send returned error: Transport retry counter exceeded
NCCL WARN connection 0x7f9c5f8 Failed to connect via ibv (last error: -110)
NCCL INFO Falling back to socket/rdma fallback for rank 2
```
chen: sounds like RDMA handshake timeouts. can you run `ibv_devinfo -v` and `rdma link` on one of the affected nodes?
maya: ran on gpu-23:
```
$ ibv_devinfo -v
hca_id: mlx5_0
transport: InfiniBand (1)
link_layer: Ethernet
phys_port_cnt: 2
port 1:
    state: PORT_ACTIVE (4)
    max_mtu: 4096
    active_mtu: 2048
    gid_table_len: 128
```
and `rdma link` shows both ports UP but counters show increasing rx errors on port 1.
netops-leo: i pulled switch counters for that rack — we had a microcode update on topo leaf-12 last week. showing some out-of-order packets and ingress drops on the VxLAN tunnel between racks 12 and 13.
sre-anna: could this be MTU/VXLAN fragmentation? RoCEv2 over UDP+VxLAN is sensitive to MTU mismatches and ECN/PFC settings.
todd: good call. check node MTU vs switch. if our node active_mtu is 2048 but vxlan overlays expect 9000, fragmentation might be dropping RDMA packets. can you run `ip link show dev eth0`?
maya: on gpu-23:
```
2: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```
so NIC is 9000 but ibv reports active_mtu 2048 for the IB port.
chen: that discrepancy indicates either the mlx5 VF/ibdev MTU negotiation fell back (maybe because of UDP offload or GID mismatch) or the IB driver was forced to a lower mtu by the switch.
netops-leo: on the switch side I see PMTU blackhole paths for vxlan between those two leafs when jumbo frames are enabled end-to-end only partially. i can force the vxlan to 1500 to test, but that will degrade nominal throughput.
maya: also observed `ibv_rc_pingpong` intermittently hangs with "transport retry counter exceeded".
infra-bot: deployment: firmware-update leaf-12 completed at 2025-11-07T02:12:44Z by netops-leo
sre-anna: short-term mitigation: set NCCL to avoid ibverbs on affected jobs so they use TCP path. e.g., export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 or set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=^ib0 to prefer eth0. downsides: CPU + socket fallback is costlier.
chen: long-term: we need to verify RoCEv2 path MTU and PFC settings. possible fixes:
- ensure switch fabric supports jumbo frames end-to-end across leaf/spine and VXLAN tunnels
- check DCB/PFC (pause frames) configuration on leafs for RDMA traffic class
- confirm NIC firmware and driver offloads for UDP checksum/segmentation are consistent
- run `ibv_devinfo -v` + `mlx5_core` logs across a failing pair to see if GID/port vlan mismatches exist
maya: test plan:
1) netops to temporarily set vxlan MTU to 1500 for leaf-12<>13 to see if drop rate drops (low risk)
2) on one failing node, disable RDMA in NCCL to confirm perf returns to socket baseline (maya)
3) collect ibv counters, `dmesg | grep mlx5` and switch ingress/egress error counters for a failing window (chen + netops-leo)
4) if MTU is the culprit, schedule a roll that makes jumbo frames consistent end-to-end and re-enable RDMA
netops-leo: starting test 1 now, will report within 15m. if that reduces packet drops we can attribute to fragmentation.
todd: if it's PFC related we'll need to coordinate with cloud provider for priority flow control on those leaf ports — might take support ticket.
maya: temporary workaround applied to the most urgent job groups: NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 and we bumped replicas to absorb slower throughput. frees up time for deeper analysis.
chen: also capture `tcpdump -i eth0 -w` on a pair and run `rdma-ndd` tools to observe UDP segmentation. i'll grab pcaps after next failure window.
sre-anna: thanks everyone. please add any artifacts (pcap, ibv outputs) to the incident ticket I created: INC-2025-4812 and tag me. we should prioritize making RoCE stable in that AZ — it's our major east-west heavy region.
maya: noted, adding logs to ticket. will update after netops confirm the vxlan MTU test.
netops-leo: vxlan MTU=1500 temporarily applied; initial counters look better, rx drops went down 93% on leaf-12. mirroring pcaps now.
chen: based on that, primary cause looks like partial jumbo support + RoCEv2 fragmentation. follow-ups: schedule end-to-end jumbo verification, or pin NCCL to socket for affected customers until we get a full fix.
maya: thanks all — marking this thread as active in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
